feedback: The geometry's balanced sensor layout and moderate size provide a solid base for the controller, allowing straightforward proportional weighting of sensors. The moderate wheel radius and track width support stable turning without excessive inertia. The integrator had to compensate with moderate PID gains to balance responsiveness and stability. The sensor size and positions appear well chosen for line detection coverage. For next iterations, I recommend trying: 1) Slightly increasing sensor size to 0.016 to improve noise robustness and line detection stability. 2) Adjusting sensor y-positions slightly forward (e.g., increase y by 0.01) to detect the line earlier and improve control anticipation. 3) Testing a slightly wider wheel track (e.g., 0.16) to enhance turning stability and reduce steering oscillation. These changes aim to improve line detection robustness and smoother control, reducing line loss and oscillation.
